items.title: Sonny Igoe interviewed by Monk Rowe, Emerson, New Jersey, July 31, 2003
items.q: So I left Woody one day and joined Tommy Dorsey two days later at the Syracuse Hotel up in Syracuse.

ctx.x: Yeah. Because the next day we were getting in the car and driving out to Nebraska on the way to meet the band, in Fall City, Nebraska I think it was. So anyway to make a long

story short, my wife got pregnant early and had to leave me on the road, she had to go home. So my father and mother found a place in North Bergen, they were building new apartments in those days and so we got an apartment over there. And when she had the baby I wanted to get time off because of the baby. And Woody wouldn’t give it to me. So I said well I’m going to have to leave the band. He says okay. So I left the band. And the last night I had with the band we were playing at Buckeye Lake, Ohio, it’s a big…

home?” I said, “six or eight miles.” He said, “well why don’t you keep it quiet, just go up there and hang around for an hour and leave.” And he said, “we’ll back you up and we’ll get your money.” And so they did, they got the money, they got the full 1200 bucks; 1200 bucks was 1200 bucks. And so they got the money for me. And so the first night I went up there Tommy was busy resetting the band, he didn’t like the way they had set it up. So my drums were on the corner. They had unloaded them. So I went over to…
